title: Credit Scores & Debt Strategy
subtitle: Learn how credit scores work and how to eliminate high-interest balances.

steps.content: A high credit score can save you tens of thousands of dollars on mortgages, auto loans, and insurance rates throughout your life.
steps.tip: Credit scores range from 300 to 850, with 740+ unlocking the best loan rates.

steps.title: The 5 Pillars of Credit Scoring
steps.content:
35% Payment History: Did you pay on time? (Most critical factor)
30% Credit Utilization: Using less than 30% of your limit
15% Length of Credit History: How long accounts have been open
10% Credit Mix: Revolving cards vs installment loans
10% New Credit Inquiries: Hard inquiries from new applications
steps.highlight: Always pay on time and keep credit utilization below 30%.

steps.question: Which single factor has the largest impact on your credit score calculation?
steps.hint: Lenders care most about whether you have a consistent track record of paying accounts on time (making up 35% of the score).

options.text: Payment history: whether you consistently pay accounts on time
options.explanation: Payment history makes up 35% of your total credit score.

options.text: The total number of credit cards in your wallet
options.explanation: Card count is minor compared to timely payments.
Income is not tracked on credit reports or scoring models.

steps.title: Debt Avalanche vs Snowball
steps.content:
Debt Avalanche: Pay minimums on all debts, then put all extra cash toward the highest interest rate debt. Mathematically saves the most money.

Debt Snowball: Pay smallest balances first for quick psychological wins.
steps.highlight: Avalanche saves the most money; Snowball builds quick psychological wins.

steps.question: How does the Debt Avalanche strategy prioritize repayments to save the most money?
steps.hint: The avalanche strategy targets the debt charging you the highest interest rate first to minimize total interest costs.

options.text: Paying off debts with the highest interest rates first
options.explanation: Attacking highest interest debt first minimizes total interest paid across the board.

options.text: Paying off the smallest dollar balance first
options.explanation: Targeting smallest balances first is the Debt Snowball method.

options.text: Paying only minimum payments on all cards forever
options.explanation: Paying minimums prolongs debt and maximizes interest expense.

steps.title: Debt Strategy Mastered
steps.content: You now understand how to safeguard your credit score and crush high-interest debt strategically.
